tldr_label: TL;DR: Chip stocks give back the Huang rally and Asia slides again, Washington readies tariffs on 16 economies, and Putin calls retaliation for refinery strikes

tldr_bullets.label: Markets
tldr_bullets.body: The Nasdaq fell 1.5% on Tuesday while the Dow closed back above 50,000. Kospi fell about 6% and Taiwan about 5% on Wednesday, ahead of today's PCE inflation report. [[TAG:danger:chip selloff]]

tldr_bullets.label: Nvidia
tldr_bullets.body: Nvidia fell about 6% a day after its 31% jump, and the semiconductor index dropped nearly 8%. Huang faces congressional hearings next week. [[TAG:warning:hearings]]

tldr_bullets.label: Tariffs
tldr_bullets.body: The US is preparing Section 301 tariffs on China, the EU and 14 others over industrial overcapacity. Reports cite rates of up to 20%, with allies capped at 15%. [[TAG:warning:trade]]

tldr_bullets.label: Ukraine
tldr_bullets.body: Putin said retaliation for Ukrainian refinery strikes is inevitable. A Russian glide-bomb attack on Zaporizhzhia killed two and wounded dozens. [[TAG:danger:escalation]]

tldr_bullets.label: Israel
tldr_bullets.body: Eisenkot agreed his first coalition deal, with Lieberman's Yisrael Beytenu, but remains short of 61 seats with a December 6 deadline. [[TAG:info:first partner]]

sections.title: Markets: Rally Fades
sections.summary: Nasdaq drops 1.5% as Dow reclaims 50,000; Asia slides again ahead of PCE data

paragraphs.heading: Tuesday Close
paragraphs.body: Cappnotes and Startup Fortune reported the Dow rose 423 points to 50,018.70 while the Nasdaq fell 1.48% to 23,733.54 and the S&P 500 slipped 0.5% to 7,201.09. Yahoo Finance described a tech sell-off and a rotation into value. BigGo reported the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell nearly 8%. [[TAG:warning:rotation]]

paragraphs.heading: Asia and the Fed
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera reported Asian markets dived Wednesday as Huang's return failed to quell AI doubts, with Kospi down 6.2%, Taiwan's Taiex 4.8% and the Nikkei 2.8%. AP, via ClickOnDetroit, reported Shanghai at a more-than-one-year low. Investinglive previewed today's October PCE report, with headline inflation seen near 3.8%, the last major reading before a December Fed decision markets expect to bring a hike. [[TAG:danger:Asia selloff]]

sections.title: Nvidia: After the Pop
sections.summary: Shares fall about 6% after 31% jump; Huang apologizes to staff ahead of hearings

paragraphs.heading: Giving It Back
paragraphs.body: CNBC reported Nvidia shares fell more than 5% as the comeback rally cooled, and Al Jazeera said the stock cooled after its surge. Startup Fortune reported chip stocks gave back the Huang rally as the semiconductor index dropped 7.9%. Yahoo Finance reported Huang apologized to employees. [[TAG:warning:volatile]]

paragraphs.heading: Hearings Ahead
paragraphs.body: Motley Fool said the real test for Nvidia could come after December 1, and KuCoin reported the stock fell ahead of Huang's congressional testimony. Reports differ on the schedule: some say Huang testifies on December 1 and 3, while others cite House committee sessions on December 1 and 2 and a Senate Banking hearing on December 3. Webtech360 reported that Trump floated a government stake, which other outlets have not yet confirmed. [[TAG:info:Dec 1-3]]

sections.title: Trade: Tariffs on 16 Economies
sections.summary: Section 301 overcapacity tariffs loom for China, EU and others; allies cite 15% cap

paragraphs.heading: The Plan
paragraphs.body: The Washington Post, citing AP sources, reported the US is ready to impose tariffs on China, the EU and others over subsidized production. Axios reported Trump is preparing a new round of targeted tariffs. Headtopics reported rates of up to 20%. Benzinga, citing the WSJ, said China could be hit hardest. Accounts of the China rate conflict. [[TAG:warning:rates unsettled]]

paragraphs.heading: Allies React
paragraphs.body: Business Upturn reported the EU, Japan and South Korea are likely to face tariffs of 15% or lower, and Aju Press said Seoul is relying on its agreed ceiling. NoCut News reported USTR would release findings on the 16 economies this week. SCMP said the tariffs are unlikely to take effect before a December summit and could become a bargaining chip. [[TAG:info:15% cap]]

sections.title: Ukraine: Retaliation Vow
sections.summary: Putin calls retaliation for refinery strikes inevitable; Zaporizhzhia strike kills two

paragraphs.heading: Putin's Warning
paragraphs.body: Al Arabiya and MLQ reported Putin said Ukraine keeps hitting Russian oil plants despite Trump's requests and that retaliation is inevitable. The Canberra Times, carrying AAP, reported Russia will respond. Reports cited industry estimates that the drone strikes have cut Russian refining volumes sharply since late October. Ukraine's foreign minister replied that Putin could end the war. [[TAG:danger:retaliation]]

paragraphs.heading: Zaporizhzhia
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera, Meduza and the Washington Post, carrying AP, reported a Russian strike on Zaporizhzhia killed two people. Injury tolls vary: Mezha cited 31, KSAT 48, and Modern Diplomacy 22. AP said Kyiv also explained its naval drone attack in Libya. [[TAG:warning:tolls vary]]

sections.title: Hormuz: Traffic Down 40%
sections.summary: Crossings fall 40% as three tankers hit in minutes; Brent stays near three-month lows

paragraphs.heading: Attacks and Traffic
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera reported Hormuz oil traffic is down 40 percent and asked whether Iran's tanker attacks are working. The figure refers to vessel crossings, not oil volumes. Maritime Executive reported three tankers were hit within minutes in the strait. Yahoo reported that Araghchi called a US land blockade of Iran impossible. [[TAG:danger:shipping]]

paragraphs.heading: Prices
paragraphs.body: Oilprice.com reported oil holding near three-month lows despite Hormuz mine claims. Marketcalls reported attacks rising while oil flows sit at about half of normal. Flow estimates differ widely across trackers. [[TAG:info:surplus]]

sections.title: Israel: First Partner
sections.summary: Eisenkot strikes first coalition deal with Lieberman; Israel kills Hamas security chief

paragraphs.heading: Coalition
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera and The New Arab reported Eisenkot secured his first coalition partner, Lieberman's Yisrael Beytenu. i24NEWS reported the deal was agreed but not yet signed, while QNC reported it signed. i24NEWS also reported the Democrats halted talks over Eisenkot's contacts with Likud. The Times of Israel reported the bloc hopes to swear in a government as soon as next Wednesday. The two parties' combined seats remain short of 61. [[TAG:info:short of 61]]

paragraphs.heading: Gaza
paragraphs.body: The Washington Post reported Israel killed Hamas's internal security chief in Gaza. Al Jazeera reported strikes killed seven as doctors warned of a meningitis outbreak, and Wafa gave the same toll. [[TAG:danger:truce strained]]
